steps.text: This matches Atomic Red Team's T1197 emulation, using BITS to download content into a .ps1 file — a classic malicious technique. I'll go with the malicious verdict and submit along with supporting artifacts.

submission.reasoning: At 06:36:43Z on workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog ran bitsadmin.exe (proc-826bdb1e01, High integrity) from an interactive cmd.exe (proc-29da349e7e). The command was `/transfer /Download /priority Foreground` and it pulled a remote file from raw.githubusercontent.com (redcanaryco atomic-red-team T1197). It saved the file as a PowerShell script, C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\bitsadmin1_flag.ps1. The BITS service host (svchost -k netsvcs -s BITS, proc-8d77a1852f) resolved raw.githubusercontent.com (conn-96c2a572b6, 151.101.208.133). It then wrote and deleted the staging file BIT9584.tmp, which is how a BITS download normally finishes. This matches MITRE T1197 (BITS Jobs), used to download a file and evade defenses by saving a script into the user's Temp folder. The URL points to an Atomic Red Team page, which suggests an emulation test, but nothing found here shows the activity was authorized, so it is treated as malicious. No later run of the .ps1 file was seen.
